utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Stand up, would you please, sir. Would you make the solemn declaration in the document which is being shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir. Perhaps, Mr. Smith, what I was waiting for was an application to amend the protective measures, because this is the rather strange situation of having facial distortion but no pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It is a unique situation, Your Honour. He's quite happy that his name be made known. It's for a particular reason that he doesn't want his face shown on the TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then, as long as everybody is aware of the situation. You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, the protective measure in relation to your image has been granted by the Court. Could you please look at a piece of paper in front of you? It contains a name and a number alongside. If you would like to refer to this individual in your testimony, could you please just use the number and not the name? Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That document will be Exhibit P427 and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Juso Taranin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how old are you?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Sixty -- no, 71.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what ethnicity are you?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you have three adult children?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In early April, 1992, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: In Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Yes, in the town of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in what neighbourhood did you live?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Gornje Polje, Branko Gagovic Street BB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how far from the centre of the town of Foca was that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, some 600 to 700 metres maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you live in a seven-storey apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did, yes, on the seventh floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many apartments were in that apartment building?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Thirty-two perhaps. I'm not quite sure but I reckon that's how many because there was a lift so I always took the lift. I never counted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of the occupants in the building, whether they were all Serb or all Muslim or 50/50, or some other?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, two, three, or four flights more is how many more Serbs were there than Muslims before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The other group was the Muslim group, is that right, people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Muslims, right. Yes, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you living with your wife at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long had you lived in the town of Foca by early April 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Since 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You lived in a village in Foca before that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The village of Brusna, Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In 1992 had you retired?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. It was in 1987 that I was retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Where did you work before you retired?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Maglic company, plywood and other timber products factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You were a machine operator there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In 1992 were you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you assigned to any military unit?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At this time did you have a weekend house in Pilipovici in Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that's a village in Foca. And about how far away from Foca town is it?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It is a village, yes, about eight kilometres, thereabouts. I'm not quite sure, but something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is that on the main road between Foca and Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, you could say that. It's not on the road directly, but you can see it. It's on a slight elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And could you see the main road from your house, your weekend house in Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I could. I could. Which leads to Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And approximately how many houses were in the village of Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: My house, my cottage was in the village, but there were very many houses in the village. I don't know how many, because there were others scattered, but many houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the main ethnicity of the people in the village?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Muslims, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was there also a JNA fuel depot in the village of Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how far from your weekend house was that JNA fuel depot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Four hundred, five hundred metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in early April 1992 were you caused to leave the Foca town to go to your weekend house in Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I was forced to go. I had reason to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court why you left Foca town and travelled to Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, the day before I left there was a lot of gunfire in the town, and we were in that building. We went downstairs to the ground floor. There were quite a number of us, both Serbs and Muslims. And that night, during the gunfire, I would go out several times when there would be a lull there, and go up to my floor, to the seventh, cast a look, see that nothing is on fire, that one can see that anything had been set on fire, but one could hear those huge detonations, and then I would go back to the cellar again, that is, to the entrance. And that is how we spent that whole night. The next day, a man who was there with me set off down to Ustikolina, and I left with him to that village of Pilipovici, and that's where I was and nobody, nothing -- we left around 10.00 and there was nobody. I couldn't see a living soul anywhere. Only a car passed by now and then. And we went through when there was no gunfire at all. There was no gunfire at all during the day. And I thus went to Pilipovici and I got to my cottage in Pilipovici. And there I spent some time, 15, 10, 15 days. I don't know how many exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can stop you there, Mr. Taranin. Do you remember what time this shooting and detonations started that night, the night before you left, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, about 10.00, 9.00, 10.00 in the evening, and then it went on all night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about what time in the morning did it cease?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, when the day began to break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you said that you went out to the -- or you looked to see where the shooting and detonations was coming from. Do you know where it was coming from?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, mostly around the town. And in those parts where we were, where I was, I could not observe any shooting near that building because it was slightly on the side towards Brod, down the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what were the residents of the building doing, the Muslims and Serbs? Were you taking -- were people taking cover?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, what I know, people worked. It was April. It was the sowing season. And I also worked around my cottage, planting potatoes, all sorts of vegetables, and people in around the village did the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm sorry, I meant during the night whilst the shooting and detonations were occurring. What were the occupants of the building doing, the apartment building that you lived in, during the night?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: During the night, those who were in the building, they were all downstairs on the ground floor in that building of mine, or perhaps somebody was -- if he was not afraid, perhaps he stayed in his flat. But I think that those were few and far between.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why were they on the ground floor? Were they seeking cover from any possible shooting or shelling?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Right, seeking shelter from shelling, from gunfire, and to see that nobody entered the building. Men were in front of the building, Serbs and Muslims both.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that morning that you left for Pilipovici. Had other Muslims left your apartment building as well?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, only that one and I, but there weren't many, no. I don't know. Only the two of us left, and my wife, because the wife and children of that other one were down there in Ustikolina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned that a friend of yours took you to Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That friend, that neighbour from the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So as far as you know, you were the only ones that left. The Muslims and the Serbs from the building stayed there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the apartment building?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you leave that morning?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I left mostly because of that -- all that gunfire and because I had my cottage down there, so because I was afraid, because I was fearful. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And before this night of shooting and shelling, did you notice any political or administrative changes in the town of Foca, in terms of the control of political or administrative facilities?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. I did notice that something was afoot, that there would be a conflict. And then I listened to Radio Foca. The parliament there was in session and they were negotiating and it was said that they could not reach an agreement not to have a conflict. It was a couple of days, a day, two days, before the gunfire started, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what date the gunfire started?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that, no, I wouldn't. No. I did not think about it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And before this night of gunfire, were there any changes in the control of the radio station or the police station or other facilities?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It was said they had taken the post office, the police, the radio station, Foca Radio, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "they," who do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Why, the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how did you hear this, this takeover of these facilities?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Radio Foca, Radio Foca, broadcast that -- because they took that over immediately that evening, before the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the relationship, the social relationships, between Muslims and Serbs before the night of the gunfire, just generally?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, it depends. They were good -- I mean, they were quite all right in my building. In my building, the relations were quite all right. They were good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Before the night of the shooting, did you see weapons being distributed to other people in your apartment building?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I saw weapons being issued to the Serbs before the shooting started, before that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who was issuing the weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know, officers, but they came in a car and issued weapons and clothes. I mean those military clothing, who wanted to take them, but they did it by surnames.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where was this happening?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: In the yard in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were you with the group that were receiving the weapons or were you in some other place? Were you in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no. I was not there. I was not exactly there. I was in the yard, on the other side of the yard. And in the entrance to the right, a car came in and they stopped there. It was all organised, distributed. They knew who to give them to by surnames. Never tried to hide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many Serbs from your apartment building did you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. receive -- did you see receive weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know the exact number but there were -- those who were -- who stood guard with me, they all had weapons in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you give an approximate number of the people that you saw that were receiving weapons? Not an exact number, but an approximate.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you: By and large, all those who were with me had weapons with them. Whether they had all come there, I don't know, but they were not hiding anything, anything. Well, what to say? There could have been about ten men with some weapons in the building, I mean, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was it -- did you see these ten men on that morning when the vehicle pulled up distributing the weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Not -- I didn't see those people really, because, you know, I moved away not to look at those people, because, you know, it wasn't simple. I mean, nobody tried to stop me, but I simply didn't feel like looking. I just realised it wasn't -- things were not good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what type of weapons were being distributed that morning, or that day?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Rifles mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was it during the day or the night that you saw this?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Late afternoon, yes, but it was daytime, daytime. Yes, afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that after the night of shooting and shelling and detonations, you went to Pilipovici and you stayed there for I think about 16 or so days. During that time what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I planted potatoes, onions, that sort of thing. I went there and dug a little around my vegetable garden and looked around me to see what was going on and trying to reckon what to do, where to go. I watched people go down on the road, go past, and I saw them towards Ustikolina. It was a column of the former detainees, former convicts, and they were also passing in cars. People went by every day towards Gorazde. They walked by from all the surrounding villages in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know what ethnicity these people were, or could you not tell?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I can't -- I couldn't tell you that. I'm not sure. I couldn't, because it was too far away, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was there a constant flow of these people going towards Gorazde over this period of time or was it sporadic?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I didn't look all the time, and it was now and then, in groups mostly. They would walk by in groups, and one could see women and children, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you receiving news as to what was occurring over this time in other parts of Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't have a radio. There was no electricity, nothing. I may have heard something from somebody. That was the only way I could learn anything; otherwise, nothing, I mean, while I was in Pilipovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after this time, did you decide to go to the JNA fuel depot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did decide that, yes, because I knew that officer and I decided to go to him. I thought that the army, the former Yugoslav one, would protect me, and that officer told me that I could be protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Without mentioning that officer's name, does his name appear on that page in front of you with the number 120? Don't say his name.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. 120, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did your wife go to the JNA fuel depot as well for protection?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Now, there was trouble with the wife. She said she would come. I left shortly before her and she stayed behind. She did not come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know the exact date that you went to the compound or the fuel depot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I can't be sure about the date. I just know that it was Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this was the Serb Orthodox Easter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the depot, were there other people like yourself seeking protection there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, there were a lot, about 70 women, men, children; 60, 70, something like that. I didn't count them, but it's somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many of them were men?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, about 20 men, approximately, adult men, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know what --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but somewhere around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know what ethnicity this group was, this group of 70?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: All were Muslims. There was only one Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were there any JNA soldiers guarding the fuel depot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that day that you arrived at the fuel depot, did some other soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. When I got in -- when I got in, there were soldiers inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And these were JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And later that day, was the fuel depot taken over by another group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Later, when they attacked that depot, there were different soldiers. They were the White Eagles and the Serb guard. There weren't any more soldiers. I don't know where they were, but they were somewhere around. At any rate, they were not in our depot where we were, the civilians. These guys came in and they kicked all of us out, out of the depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say they kicked you out of the depot, did they kick you out of a building that you were being protected in within this JNA depot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Out of that hangar, warehouse, depot, whatever you call it. It was a hangar, I guess, for vehicles. It was something like an underground thing. And then when they kicked us out, we all went out. They made us all line up and put our hands up. As for the women and children, they returned them into this depot and they started beating us, mistreating us. They forced us to sing. They searched us. They took away whatever people had: money, gold. First they made us take everything out of our pockets, then they searched us. So they mistreated us there for about two or three hours, beat us. They even shot some people. Things like that. Cursed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How many people did they shoot?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I know the names of two of them, but they killed about five or six or seven people, I believe. But I only know two. They were from a village there. I did not know everybody who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how were these people selected for the shooting?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: An officer came and he pulled out some piece of paper, and then he started calling out names. And then, when he would call out various names, and then when he would ask, "Who is that to you?" And if this person would say it was his son, then he would make him lie on the ground immediately, on his stomach. When he would order that, when he finished this roll-call, then they got these people up and then they took us about 10 metres away from us and they executed them. They shot them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: After these people were shot, did you notice whether they in fact had been killed?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. I couldn't. I couldn't see that. All of them lay there. I couldn't notice, and we didn't dare look either. "Hands up," and we had to look at them only. It wasn't that there was one of them only. There were about 20 of them, of these White Eagles, and these members of the Serb guard. Because that's what it said on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And these White Eagles, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, judging by the dialect, it seems that they were from Serbia. As far as I could see by their dialect, by the way they spoke, you know -- you know what dialect is. When they curse at you, when they cuss at you, when they say bad things to each other, I understand by this dialect that they were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were you yourself personally mistreated?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Even put a knife to my throat. And he said to me, "What are you going to do if I slaughter you now?" And I just looked him in the eye, nothing else, and then he turned his knife around and he put it back in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after this shooting, you mentioned that you were at the depot for about two or three hours. Were you taken to KP Dom in Foca that day?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that day, that day. That day when they finished whatever they had to do, what -- I mean this mistreatment, these killings, how should I know? Then he ordered us to go in front of this administration building where this officer was. He ordered us all to go there. He said that a bus would come and if anybody would try to run away, he'd be killed on the spot. Then we waited there for a while and two buses came. They put us into one bus and they were in the other bus. This other bus was for them and probably for those soldiers. I didn't see all of this. I just saw our bus being loaded. One stood in front -- at the front door and the other one stood by the back door. So there is an entrance and there is an exit, so one stood in front and the other one stood in the back, and that's how we left. But we did take about two or three hours to reach Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we can just go back a moment, what were the names of the two people that you knew were killed?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Salko Sehovic and Dedovic, Dedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can't remember the first name, that's okay. How old was Dedovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Meho, Meho, Meho Dedovic. He was an elderly man, pretty old, over 80, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Salko Sehovic, how old was he?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say. Probably my age or perhaps a few years younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you all got on the bus, on one bus. Was that all of the refugees --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- at this fuel depot, except for the ones that were killed?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Everybody, everybody, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And on the way to the KP Dom, did you pass by a village named Paunci?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: A village of Paunci. It was all afire. All the houses were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was that a Serb or a Muslim village, do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It was a Muslim village but there were two Serb houses as well -- no, three. Two or three Serb houses, but at the very beginning of the village. I know when I went out for the week -- for weekends, I know that I passed by them. There was also a servicing station for cars, for repairing cars, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many houses did you see on fire in this village?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, how can I know? I mean, I just saw them on fire. How could I know how many? Because what could I think about? I just thought, let them kill me so that I don't suffer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And on the way to the KP Dom in Foca, did you stop at Velecevo women's prison?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, about half an hour, perhaps. I can't say for sure but we were there for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know why you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then after this half an hour, you were taken to the KP Dom in Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you arrived at the KP Dom or the entrance to the KP Dom, did you see anyone else there outside of the prison?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: We did not. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how many soldiers were guarding you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Two. I saw two soldiers, one in the front and one in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were they the soldiers that took over the depot at Pilipovici?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no. I mean, it was these White Eagles and the guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the two people on the bus -- sorry, it was two members of the White Eagles that -- or the guards that were guarding you on the bus; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you got to the KP Dom's entrance, were you handed over to anyone, to any other guards or police or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They made us go out. They said the men should go out. They took us out, they lined us up, and the police came out of the KP Dom and took us over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: These police that came out of the KP Dom, do you remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Police uniforms, and they carried batons and pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what colour were these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What colour were the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, the uniforms were bluish, greenish, I mean darkish. You know, like they wore before, like policemen wore before, KP Dom policemen. It was the same like that previous uniform, bluish, greenish, sort of a petrol colour. Well, it would be hard for me to say with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "KP Dom policemen," do you mean KP Dom guards or special police attached?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Guards, guards, guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long were you kept outside the KP Dom before you went inside?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I thought there were -- it was 10 or 15 minutes, 15 at the most, because this policeman said, "Had they been searched?" And they said yes. And then he said, "Take them in there." And that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were the women and children taken inside as well?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did not see. I did not see. They drove us up -- they drove them up there too, but they didn't come in with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you went inside with the other men, about 20, is that right? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And once were you taken inside the building, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Nothing. The policemen -- I mean, the guards took us into a building, the first building there by the entrance. Then we went upstairs. He opened the door. We walked in and we found lots of prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many prisoners were in this place where you were bought to?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: There were a lot. I can't say for sure, but I think there were about 100 of them, certainly; I mean, over there in that building, that ground floor where they -- those ground floor rooms where they brought us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was this a separate building to the building that you initially went in when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, there was a separate entrance. There was a separate entrance, into the building, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you went into this separate entrance, did you have to go up any stairs or was the room that you were taken to on the same floor of the entrance?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The building is a bit high up, higher than the entrance into the KP Dom itself. There are some steps. So then when you enter the building, there aren't any stairs, or at least I can't remember that there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you went in that entrance, did you turn left or right to go to this room where it was quite crowded?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can ask that P88 - it's the sketch of the KP Dom - be shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if you could point on that sketch, point to the building or the entrance that you were taken to before you got to the room and where you saw those large number of prisoners. Take your time to have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I'm not very knowledgeable about these drawings and things like that, but I'll try to show you whatever you ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can look at the map. Does that look familiar to you in relation to the layout of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say "map," do you mean the sketch or is he also meant to be looking at the plan, Exhibit 6?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It does look like it. It does look like it. Sketch, I'm not very good at that kind of thing. I'm not very good at that kind of thing. But if I'm not 100 per cent sure, I'll tell you. This is the entrance, here. You walk by this building, this is where the entrance is, and then you go here, and then -- and then you enter this building here, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: You turn to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, he indicates the entrance to building A and had the pointer moving towards the left on the ground floor. I did mean sketch, not map, and he's unfamiliar with the map, so that's why we're using the sketch, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And as you entered the entrance, you didn't go up any stairs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we came in front of the building, yes. But then when we entered the building, no, no. I can't remember, perhaps, but there weren't any stairs. Perhaps there were about two stairs, one or two, but I can't remember. Because until then, I had never, ever in my life entered that KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness. For the record, Your Honour, I believe the witness is referring to Room 11 on the plan 6/2A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad you think so, or you believe so. It's anything but clear, if I may say so. I don't suppose we need worry unless there's some real issue taken about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the people that were in this room, were they Muslims, that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: All were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long did you spend in this room?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I spent two nights in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In this room were most people sleeping on the floor or on beds?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I slept on the floor, but there were a lot on tables, on the floor. I don't know. Those who came in first managed to get a hold of the beds and then there weren't any beds left, so those who came later slept on the floor or on tables. There were also some benches, so they could sleep there too. But then we slept between the beds. That's where we slept, depending on where each person found some room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And whilst you were in these two rooms - sorry - whilst you were in this room over these two nights, did any people from outside of the KP Dom come and question you about the conditions that you were living in?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, nobody. Actually, two women came. Two women came when I spent those two nights in that room. On the next day, two women came, and one looked like some kind of a translator or something. You could see this red cross. There was a red cross on their uniforms. And they asked, "Is this the way you sleep?" And some people said, "Yes, that's where we sleep, down here." A policeman brought them in, a guard, that is, and then she told the policeman that he had to go out. And then he answered back. He said, "You go out," and they had to go out and he went with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long were they there for asking about the conditions before they were told to leave?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, they were there for five minutes, not even that long. Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after you were in this room for a couple of nights, were you moved to another room?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. The next day a guard came and transferred all of us, all of us who had come from Pilipovici - and I don't know who else was there - transferred us all to this other building right next to this one. The same kind of room. The rooms that we were transferred to were just like the rooms that we had been in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if P88 could be put in front of the witness again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, can you just point with the pointer on the entrance that you went into to get to the second --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: From this building, we went to -- from that building we went to this building here, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if you could place the pointer on the entrance that you went into, into that second building, on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not really good at this. If I were there, I could show you easily. But we came to this building. We moved to this building. Now, is it this one? But it was the adjacent building. It was -- they were right next to one another. We just came from this one and we walked in a straight line and came to another building like this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you go to the building that is marked B, the entrance to the building marked B? If you can look at the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I could not say that, because I never gave it a thought, the number of the building or anything, never paid any attention to things like that, never. Whether it's B or C or D, never paid any attention, and I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: This second building that you went into, once you went into the entrance of that building, was the room that you went into on the same floor or on a higher floor than the entrance?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Again, a ground-floor room, a ground-floor room. As soon as you enter the building, just as you enter the building, to the left, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. We're finished with the map. Thank you. Sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you were taken into this room, were there any other detainees in that room when you arrived, other than the group you arrived with?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I suppose so. There must have been other detainees. Must have been, because less than 55 of us moved house; and yes, we were 55 at the time of the roll-call that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And just to be clear, the group that you left -- that you left with from the first room, was that the group of 20 that you arrived with at the KP Dom, approximately 20?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, yes. You could say that practically almost all of those from Pilipovici who arrived with me, yes, they almost all of them came to that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the total number, including this group, that you arrived with was 55 in the second room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening, when they lined us up and then roll-called us, each one of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of the group in this room, of 55?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Muslims, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how long did you stay in this second room?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Ten, 15 days I was there, thereabouts. I'm not sure, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you were released from the KP Dom after this?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken for interrogation to the investigator, and I was at the investigator's. And after two days, that is on the third day, I was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who interrogated you at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I've never -- I never saw that man whilst a civilian but the detainees -- detainees told me that he was now -- what was it, Koprivica, that was Koprivica, nice young man, quite young, but I never knew him until that day. I never set my eyes on him. I don't know his first name. The last name is Koprivica. And they said -- and I was told that he was Koprivica. I didn't know him and he also said so when interrogating me. He gave me his full name but I just didn't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what questions were you asked by him?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: When I entered, it was, "Good morning" -- "Good day," "Good day." "Want to smoke?" "No, I don't smoke, thank you." "First name, last name." And then he asked me, "Where is your weapon?" "Father's name." He says, "Where is your weapon? What party were you a member of?" "None." "Where is your weapon?" "Never had weapons in my life." And so he went on for a while, and when I said Juso Taranin, then he asked me, "And what is Mensa Taranin to you?" I said she was my daughter. And then he changed his opinion about me and stopped provoking me. He picked up the typewriter and wrote and said, "Is this okay?" "It is." "Sign it."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you ask him for help to get you out of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't. All he said was, "Well, if I can help you, I will."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where were you interrogated? Which building?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: That building that I went in when I was brought there. From the yard, I went into it and then up those stairs, and I started upstream, the Drina by passage, and I reached an office. And I had a guard because a guard was with me all the time. And he came to the penitentiary, called out my name, took me with him, and I followed him, and took me in front of the office, and he told me to stand there and wait there, and he waited too. And when this man came out, Koprivica, then I went into his office, and the guard left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did the guard take you back to your room after the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did. When I -- when my interrogation was over, the guard came again and took me back to the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what colour uniform was the guard wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Like all the guards, they all had the same kind of uniforms. Like the first -- like all the uniforms, they were not different uniforms, the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Oh, it was greenish-blue, something like that flag over there, looks like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the United Nations flag, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can't see the green.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean the colour. The colour I mean. Looked like it. Perhaps a bit lighter or perhaps darker. I'm not really good at colours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps for all our memories, the record should record that it is the usual United Nations sky-blue flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were other detainees interrogated like yourself whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Except I don't know if it was Koprivica. I did not see who interrogated them, nor did we talk much about who interrogated you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many people from your room were taken for interrogation every day, if it happened every day?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, not every day. Not in my room. In my room, no, it didn't happen every day. Two or three per day, now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "two or three per day," is that two or three from the whole detention centre, taken for interview, for interrogation, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know. I did not see other rooms. I could see only who went from my room. Couldn't see anything outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So you're saying that about two or three would be taken from your room on certain days but not every day?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no, not every day, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom, did you see any detainees with recent injuries on them?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can think carefully, for the time that you were there, about how many people did you see with recent injuries?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I saw some three or four men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know the names of any of these men? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I do know, yes. I know one. Rahman Taib.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Rahman Taib?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, Rahman Taib.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What injuries did he have?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Oh, he had horrible injuries on his face and head and back, and we used some damp, some wet rags to put on him. I don't know if he survived, I don't know. But I was there. I wondered if he would live, but he was still alive when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you describe what the injuries looked like?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He was all black. His eyes were all swollen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: From his injuries, could you tell how he was injured?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Beating, blows with rifles, I mean rifle butts, batons, boots, what do I know? On the back, we took -- we took his clothes off him and then put wet rags on his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did he tell you or anyone else how he received those injuries?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no, did not say anything. He did -- no, nobody talked. We were afraid that perhaps one of us might be a snitch, so nobody talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know where he received those injuries, either inside or outside the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you first saw him at the KP Dom, did he have the injuries or did he not have them?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He did not have them. He did not have the injuries when I saw him first in the KP Dom, the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And which room did you see him in? Was it the first room or the second room?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The second room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long after the first time when you saw him with no injuries did you see him the next time with injuries?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. Two, three days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was any medical treatment offered to him by the guards, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Never. A guard never entered except when they wanted to take us for breakfast or lunch or dinner. The guard never entered. And in the evenings when they roll-called us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And apart from the treatment that other detainees from your room were giving Mr. Rahman, was any other treatment given to him whilst you were at the KP Dom, medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, nothing. Nobody entered while I was there. After that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you saw about three or four people with recent injuries. Can you describe any of the injuries on the other people that you saw, these other two or three?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I know that one had his arm broken, and another one or two of them were badly beaten, not like Rahman, but they were all -- but they had been beaten, and that one had his arm broken and he always held it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person that had his arm broken?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't. I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you first saw him --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: And even had I known it, I would have forgotten it by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you first saw him at the KP Dom, was the arm broken or was it normal?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I did not see him before when his arm wasn't broken, but what happened when he came, it was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know how he received this broken arm?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, I don't know how it happened. I simply could see that he could not use it, that it was just like that. He could not use it. He couldn't do anything with it. And he said that this bone here had been broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicated the left forearm and placed it across the front of his body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know whether he received this broken arm before he arrived at the KP Dom or whilst he was there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, it wasn't broken before, when he arrived, when he went there for interrogation or wherever. I don't know. You just don't know. I mean, your name is called out and -- I don't know where he was, whether he was -- he had been to interrogation or what. I don't know. All you see: He's just brought into the room, called out, goes out of the room, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how do you know it wasn't broken before he arrived at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Because I was in the room with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was any treatment given to him by the authorities at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. No. No, not while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did he do anything for his injury or did other detainees try and give some treatment for the injuries? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, he tore his shirt and wrapped it around and held his arm like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was the skin broken on the arm or was it --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't come close to look. No, I didn't. I didn't come close at all. It was those young -- those who knew better, what and how to do, it's they who did it. I didn't come close. And he slept in the other corner of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you notice a man whilst you were at the KP Dom with a badly injured head?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know that person's name?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you describe the injury to his head?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, you know, he was struck here on the head, and this blood that was there, it was never washed off; it was never cleaned. I saw him in the room. Later on, others, I mean detainees, cleaned it and put some cloth over it to stop bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the right rear of his head and the right side of his face with his right hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did he say how he received that injury?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you first saw this man at the KP Dom, did he have the injury or not?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He did not have the injury when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned that there were another two or so detainees that you saw were beaten, but not as badly as Taib Rahman.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, they didn't. Yes, this one with his broken arm, but nobody was beaten like Rahman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom - I'll only ask a few questions on this, Your Honour - but did you get enough food to eat?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The food was horrible. I don't know how those people who were there longer managed it. I wasn't there long, but if the food was that bad all the time, I doubt if I would survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you lose weight whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did. Yes, I did lose some weight. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you receive enough food whilst you were there? You stated that it was horrible, but did you receive enough?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: You get a cup of tea in the morning; at noon you get a small pot like this, you get some pasta or some potatoes or perhaps rice; and tea in the evening, and a slice of bread, one bite.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicated with his hands a cup-size area when he was describing the amount of food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know who the warden of the KP Dom was whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I did not. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you informed by other detainees who the warden of the KP Dom was whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that he did not know who was the warden while he was there, and the next question is whether other prisoners told you that. And the witness said that he did not know while he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He said that he did not know whilst he was there. Now, it depends, I suppose, what the meaning of the word "know" is. But he's then asked, "Were you informed by anybody else?" What's the problem? He's actually answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is what I'm saying, that he did not know, and my interpretation of this is that he was not informed, that he had no knowledge about the identity of the warden, if he says that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That may be your interpretation, but the Prosecution is not bound by your interpretation. That's what I said. It depends upon the word "know." He's already answered it, and if this question was not pursued any further, we would be left with a contradiction on the record. That would be a nonsense, if I may say so. You proceed, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have personal knowledge of who the warden was whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Could he be asked: Did he see anybody or something? This is what the difference is, is it not? You are relying upon the word "know" as having from his own perceptions known. Well, why don't you ask questions which are directed to that, and then we can go into the hearsay part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you see the warden whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you told by other detainees who the warden was whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They spoke about it. They said they knew who that was. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did they tell you who the warden was or not?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They said it was some Kunarac, I don't know. I didn't see him. I didn't know. And I don't know that man. I don't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I suggest to you, Mr. Smith, that now that the hearsay evidence is in, it is of so little weight that we should not waste any further time on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. And it is time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned after about 10 or 15 days after you arrived in the second room at the KP Dom you were released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Who was the first to tell you that you would be released?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Nobody told me. When the guard took me out -- I mean, when I came to where they were in the guards' hut at the entrance, Slavko Koroman - he was a guard, policeman, whatever - he said that I was free to go, that I was released, whatever, because I knew him from before, in the civilian days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did Slavko Koroman used to work at the KP Dom before the war?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, he appears at number 32 on Exhibit P3, which is the list of the guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He just said that I was free to go. And I said to him, "Where should I go?" Because the entire town was in flames, so to speak. There was shooting. And also when I went out, I saw some other prisoners whom I knew from before. I saw them standing there in front of the building, and then we went through town together, and I came to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did he give you a certificate when you left the KP Dom, confirming your stay there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He gave me a certificate, and I gave it to you. You've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: With the help of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can look at the certificate now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a copy of the certificate on Prosecution identification number 94 -- sorry. In fact, it's the original certificate but you have it as number 94 and 94A. We have provided some extra copies to the Registry -- I mean not the Registry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Assuming that it goes into evidence, does it have to be under seal? Because it doesn't seem to reveal anything other than his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the tender of this, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the original of this document will be exhibit P94 and the English translation will be P94A.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: On that release paper, it states that you had to report to the police station every day, the Serbian -- the police station of the Serbian Foca municipality. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, every day, every day. I reported to the police in the morning, every day, because Slavko told me that I had to report to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. police every day, and it says so here too. And when I would come to the police, I would have to tell them the number, 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, that certificate has the date that you were kept at the KP Dom as the 18th of April until the 3rd of May, 1992. Do you know whether those dates are correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no. They are not correct. I'm not sure, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Also on that --

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: And I really wouldn't know the dates, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you recognise any signatures on that confirmation document?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't really recognise it, but in my opinion, it seems to me that this last signature here is Koroman's, that Koroman. I'm not sure. That is just what I think. Because I'm not that literate. I can't tell signatures apart very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Which signature are you referring to? Is that number 3, underneath the authorised employees of the Serbian Foca Police Station?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Number 3, signature number 3. I mean, I'm not sure, and I can't say for sure that it is his signature, but I guess it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you guess it's the signature of Mr. Koroman, is that right, or is it someone else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it really worth pursuing this, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Koprivica, Koprivica. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I mean, what's the weight of it? He's illiterate and he can only say he's guessing. Now, what's the weight of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I think he said slightly more than guessing, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but if you read his evidence as a whole, you'll see that he's really guessing. Do you think we could move on to something that he can give evidence about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom, were you ever told why you were detained there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, never. No, no one ever told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said you went back to your apartment. About how long did you stay in the town of Foca at your apartment? For about how many months?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I stayed from the day of my release until the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you stay with your wife during this time in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, with my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you reported to the police station daily. Who in particular did you report to? Was there any individual that you had to report to?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The duty policeman, the town policeman on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did you have to do when you reported? Was it sign a card or was there something more involved than that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Nothing. I just had to tell him number 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So your reporting at the police station was only for a very short moment every day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: As soon as I'd walk in and say "number 15," I could leave immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were other people obliged to report to the police station?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were released from the KP Dom had to report, all of them, because those who came to the police station told me, in front of the police station, that they were coming the same way that I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many other people did you know were required to report to the police?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: We came from various parts of town, so I can't really tell you how many. Everybody tried to leave before there were many soldiers and policemen in town. You wanted to go there and to come back as soon as possible, as quickly as possible, so you couldn't really see very much. The policemen -- a policeman, if he would see me, would always ask me why I was going out, because Muslims were forbidden to go out. And then I would show him this certificate and then he would always tell me, "The faster you go, the better for you." And also he would tell me, "Take the same route you took on your way out. Go back the same way."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were the police at this police station?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: All of them Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the other people that were required to report to the police station that you knew, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The ones I know were Muslims, and those who I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know of any Serb men that were required to report to the police station during this time?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that as you were going to the police station or coming back, a policeman once said to you that Muslims were forbidden to go out. Had you heard that before, before that policeman said that to you?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I heard that before through this loudspeaker that was taken round town on a car, where it said that Muslims were forbidden from going about town and whoever would be caught would be punished severely. That was repeated several times for several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who did that car belong to? Did it have any markings on it? Who was actually making these announcements?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know who was in the car. There was a man, though. But the car belonged to the Foca radio station, if you look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you hear these announcements of Muslims not being able to leave their house on the radio as well or not?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I heard it on the radio too, but this loudspeaker was separate from that, because on the radio you could hear things only at a given point in time. You would turn on the radio and you would hear certain things at a certain time but -- in your apartment, but then this loudspeaker you could hear it all over town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know who was making these announcements on the radio? Any particular individual?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when did you first start to hear that Muslims were not able to leave their houses? When did you first hear this car or these radio messages?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: When I got out of the KP Dom, we were allowed to move about for a few days, four or five days, and then when this loudspeaker came up, and also all of this that was heard on the radio, that was it. Whoever would go out would be liquidated overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you hear that message that whoever would go out would be liquidated overnight over the radio or from the car or is that your assumption?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The radio station. I heard them say that whoever is caught going out will be punished most severely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was that being referred to -- were they referring to Muslims and Serbs or just one of the groups?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Over the radio, it said the Muslims only.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the Muslims that you knew that were in Foca at that time, were they abiding by this order?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I abided by that, but I cannot guarantee whether the others did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was your apartment searched during this period, after your release from KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, twice, the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the reason for them searching your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They were searching for a radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was there one there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really know what that was, frankly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know whether other Muslim apartments were searched during this period?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: On my floor, there was a Muslim, and, yes, his apartment was searched too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what about Serb apartments? Were Serb apartments in your building searched; do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How did you get food during this time? Before you left Foca and after you left the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, there was war and there was this inflation, and then for a certain period of time, some of my Serb neighbours brought me things. They offered things to me, and that's how we managed to survive. We cooked in the apartment, and we saved up so that we could eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the food that you had during this period, was it different, in terms of quality and quantity, to the food that you received at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, it was different but, you know, it was far better. You know, you could buy things if you had the money to do so, if you would give money to, say, a Serb kid, a child, who would go out, then he could get things for you at the shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: During this period that you were in Foca, how were you treated once you were released from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, as far as the building is concerned, there were some leaders there in the building, so nobody -- I mean, they didn't come to see me lately but they didn't treat me badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were the Muslims that were living in the apartment building before the war, were they still living there when you were released?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no. Very few of them. Three or four families were there in that entire building altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know where the other families had gone?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were the Serb families that were there before the war, were they in the building when you were released from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were all in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were threats made to people of Muslim ethnicity to leave Foca after you were released from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, that there would be buses and that we'd have to leave. That's what a Serb told me. A Serb told me not to tell anyone, though, that there would be buses, but that I shouldn't tell anyone, that my wife should go and get a certificate and that we should go to Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did your wife -- did your wife get a certificate?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. She went to the police and they gave her this certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did the certificate say?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I can't tell, really. I don't know. I didn't keep it. I mean, just for as long as I got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where did she get the certificate from?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: From the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the police station where you reported?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, you know, my wife went, and I think there was some kind of a special point where these certificates were given. But at any rate, they were issued by officials who worked at the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that Muslims from your apartment building had left when you were released from the KP Dom. Were Muslims from other parts of the town leaving as well? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, probably. Probably, yes, but I could not know that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you mentioned that you left Foca on the 4th of July, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
